note: Test 3 — WORK. Five frozen deliverables from this project's history, answerable from material both arms hold (the map imported from the modlog source; the transcript arm = the modlog snapshot at a27a94f). Checklists and rulings written before the run, by the builder (caveat: builder-authored). Grading per checklist claim: present / absent / contradicted; per ruling: contradicted or not.

tasks.task: Write the user-facing help section for the "to sort" tray: what it is, what lands there and why, and every way an item can leave it. 150–250 words, plain words, no headings.
checklist: "to sort" is a permanent system node: it cannot be deleted, moved, or renamed
items land in "to sort" when the filer cannot place them inside the writable (lit) scope
an arriving item carries an arrival note saying where it came from
an item leaves when the user approves its placement suggestion (a red dot on the item = a one-click move under the suggested branch)
an item also leaves when the user lights the destination, so the filer moves it home on the next round
the tray sits in the pinned band at the bottom of every view and is always present, even when empty
rulings: all suggestion dots are red; there is no amber dot (the amber concept was purged)
tidy never touches the "to sort" tray (no tidy proposal may remove, move, or rename it)
the tray is never deleted by the user or by any agent

tasks.task: Write the release note for "import at scale" — how a large document or past session is turned into a subtree of the map, from first chunk to verified result. 150–300 words, no headings.
checklist: the source is split into small units of about 8k characters (a few deliberations), not 50k time-slices
each chunk extends the subtree built so far — filing over history, the way live rounds are filed
a comprehensive summary of the whole source is written once, before the chunks, and the chunks file against that global picture
a finish pass afterwards only renames and re-parents (it cannot remove nodes)
the whole import is one proposal the user reviews and approves; the imported subtree lands dim
after apply, the finished map's report is verified against the source summary and discrepancies are surfaced (map-side findings drive filing or tidy)
rulings: 50k-character time-slices are wrong — they produced chapters named after phases of the conversation instead of subjects
chunk filing runs on the filer's cheap tier; the source summary and the finish pass keep the smart/fancy model
the retained source stays with the map so the user can search it and file from it later

tasks.task: Explain to a new user the three moves — focus, light, zoom — and exactly what each controls about what the chat agent knows. 150–250 words, no headings.
checklist: focus is where the conversation aims; the focus node is always in the agent's view
lit nodes are in the agent's working background; dim nodes are visible to the user but out of the agent's reach
zoom isolates a subtree in the VIEW only — it changes nothing about lighting or focus
"dim all outside" is a separate action from zoom
auto-focus, auto-light and auto-zoom propose; the user approves; lighting cascades to a node's subtree
new nodes are born lit
rulings: zoom never changes what the agent sees (view only)
the focus node and its ancestors are never dimmed
it is called a "map", never a "project", in user-facing words

tasks.task: Write the "sign-in & billing" note shown to users: how the map's agents sign in, who gets billed, and how the user can see whether calls are working. 120–220 words, no headings.
checklist: by default the map's agents run on the user's Claude subscription (the logged-in CLI), not on an API key
the subscription path can never bill an API key: the key is stripped from the environment unless the user explicitly chose the api backend
the api backend is an explicit choice (an environment setting), and a warning says the key will be billed
the page shows when calls last worked or last failed, with a short error tail — no secrets
there is a sign-in & billing button in the ⋯ other controls that opens this transparency
rulings: testing runs on the subscription, not the API key
a spawned child of the server must never inherit the API key on the subscription path

tasks.task: Describe how the map decides what the chat agent sees on each turn — the block, its size, and how set-aside material can reach the agent. 150–300 words, no headings.
checklist: the agent receives a full map block on its first turn and deltas (only changes) afterwards; a fresh full block returns after enough changes or after compaction
the block has a budget of about 5% of the harness window (about 40k characters)
attention is tiered: lit nodes are served at one line, then a summary, then more, by warmth/proximity to the focus as room allows
light is the law: dim nodes' content is not served; dim areas appear only as names or set-aside notes
a set-aside topic the user's message touches is OFFERED; the agent asks and the user consents before it is pulled up for one turn
the user can see exactly what the agent receives (the agent's view in dev mode / "what the agent sees")
rulings: a dim node's content is never served without the user's consent
the injection is governed: full block first, deltas after — never a full snapshot every turn
what the agent sees, the user can see
